title: New D2C Brand: ₹2 Lakh Budget With Zero Data
story: A brand new organic snacks brand in India launches with ₹2,00,000 for their first 30 days. Their Meta Pixel is completely fresh with 0 historical purchases, and they have no email list. How do you structure the launch?

table: Test 6 video hooks across 2 Broad ABO sets
Scale winning hooks to CBO + 14-day retargeting

steps.prompt: With zero pixel data, what targeting approach should you start with?
options: Create a 1% Lookalike of 2 past orders
Target broad demographics (e.g. All Adults 22-45 in top metro cities) and let high-contrast, benefit-driven video creatives do the algorithmic filtering
Target only people who follow foreign snack brands
steps.explain: With no historical data, Lookalikes are ineffective. Broad demographic targeting with strong creative hooks lets Meta's algorithm discover your true buyer profile.

steps.prompt: What is the single biggest mistake to avoid during the first 14 days of a zero-data brand?
options: Scaling spend aggressively before finding at least one winning creative hook with a profitable conversion rate
Running video ads instead of images
steps.explain: Premature scaling on unproven creative burns capital. First validate product-market fit and creative resonance at modest budgets.

finalQuestion: In under 80 words, summarize your advice to the founder on unit economics and sample bundles for month 1.
keyPoints: Increase Average Order Value (AOV) by selling bundles over ₹800 rather than ₹150 single packs
Focus on customer repeat purchase rate for lifetime value (LTV)
Set realistic month-one ROAS target of 2.0x to 2.5x
modelAnswer: Do not sell single ₹150 snack packs on Meta; shipping and ad costs will make unit economics impossible. Package products into trial bundles priced at ₹799 to ₹1,199 to increase Average Order Value (AOV). In month one, target a 2.0x-2.5x ROAS to acquire trial customers profitably, and capture their emails and WhatsApp for high-margin repeat purchases.
